name: Ad-tech frequency cap / IVT detection
parent_research_topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Two complementary incumbent layers. (a) Infrastructure / feature-backend layer: Aerospike is the runaway default for ad-tech feature, profile and cap stores (Trade Desk publicly serves data in 8 ms with Aerospike and cut server count ~80% scaling from 15B to 90B auctions/day; Criteo handles 950B requests/day at 50 ms p99 and 25M tx/s, having reduced hardware 78% migrating from Couchbase+Memcached; documented public customers include MGID, fuboTV, Yahoo, AppLovin-adjacent). Redis / Redis Enterprise and now Valkey are the broad mid-market default for cap-counter+Lua patterns (AWS Architecture Blog's 'Serving Billions of Ads in Just 100 ms' uses ElastiCache). ScyllaDB / Cassandra / Couchbase appear in legacy stacks. Generic feature stores: Tecton (Databricks-acquired Aug 2025, ~$900M valuation), Fennel (Databricks-acquired Apr 2025, Rust-based, explicitly markets to ad-tech), Chalk, Hopsworks, Feast-on-Redis. Streaming: Apache Flink, RisingWave, Materialize for pacing analytics, but not on the inline cap path. In-house Rust/C++ on RocksDB/Sled common at top end. (b) Domain anti-fraud / IVT product layer: HUMAN Security (MediaGuard pre-bid IVT, verified 20T+ digital interactions/week, flagged 10T+ IVT requests in 2025 alone), DoubleVerify (DV), Integral Ad Science (IAS), Pixalate, TrafficGuard, Spider AF, ClickCease, Anura, Fraud Blocker, Lunio, mFilterIt, Fraudlogix. CTV-specific: HUMAN MediaGuard, Pixalate CTV Compliance, FreeWheel/SpringServe/Publica with built-in household-level capping.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Frequency capping (in-house at the ad server): Google Ad Manager / DV360, Amazon DSP, Meta, FreeWheel (CTV publisher suite, household-level), SpringServe (Magnite, Apr-2025 next-gen platform in closed beta with Disney/Paramount/Roku/Samsung/WBD), Publica, Yospace SGAI, Kevel (retail-media API-first), AdGlare, AdButler, Roku Ad Manager. IVT / click fraud detection: HUMAN Security (Goldman Sachs-owned; raised $50M+ in Oct 2024 led by WestCap, ~$300M total raised; partnered with Primis Apr 2025 for pre-bid filtering), DoubleVerify (NYSE:DV; acquired Scibids for $125M in 2023; reported 101% YoY North America bot-fraud surge in its 2025 Global Insights Report based on 1T+ impressions; 140% surge in CTV fraud schemes Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025; 10x more fraudulent CTV apps detected in 2025), IAS (NASDAQ:IAS; Q3 2025 revenue $154.4M +16% YoY; entered $1.4B+ definitive acquisition agreement with Novacap Sep 24 2025), Pixalate (smaller, ~$4.4M revenue 2024, MRC-accredited, integrated into Amazon DSP and MoPub; Q3 2025 benchmarks: 21% web IVT, 33% mobile-app IVT, 19% CTV IVT), TrafficGuard (ASX-listed, 1T+ data points/month, mobile MMP-native), ClickCease (CHEQ-owned since 2020, 14k+ customers, SMB segment), Spider AF (30+ ad networks, $150-375/month tiers), MMP-internal: AppsFlyer Protect360 (trained on 500B+ events), Adjust Fraud Prevention Suite 2.0 (~2T events/month), Branch, Kochava Fraud Console, Singular. Edge bot/fraud: Castle (Cloudflare Worker integration May 2025), DataDome, PerimeterX (HUMAN-owned), Arkose Labs, Kasada, Cloudflare Bot Management, Fastly, Imperva, Akamai.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed but tilted commercial. Aerospike Community Edition is AGPLv3 (a real adoption deterrent for many enterprises); Enterprise Edition is closed-source, volume-licensed. Redis 8.0+ is AGPLv3 (after the 2024 SSPL detour); Valkey is BSD 3-Clause and is now the cloud-default fork (Ubuntu 26.04 ships it as the redis package, AWS ElastiCache supports it). Tecton, Fennel, Chalk, Hopsworks are proprietary / managed (Tecton and Fennel now wholly owned by Databricks). HUMAN, DV, IAS, Pixalate, TrafficGuard are 100% proprietary SaaS. Kevel, AdGlare, AdButler are proprietary. Beava's Apache-2.0 is the cleanest license posture in the segment but the OSS axis is not the dominant buyer filter here - operational scale and IVT-classification accuracy are.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: High. The 'good enough' alternative is bundled into multiple hyperscaler/platform subscriptions a buyer already pays: (1) AWS ElastiCache (Valkey/Redis) plus the AWS RTB Fabric reference architecture covers the cap-counter half; (2) Google Ad Manager / DV360 bundle frequency capping natively for buy-side spend; (3) Amazon DSP integrates Pixalate for pre-bid IVT; (4) Databricks now controls Tecton+Fennel for the feature-store half; (5) Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects + Bot Management + Castle integration covers edge frequency cap and bot detection for publisher/edge use cases. The IVT-classification SIVT layer (HUMAN, DV, IAS, Pixalate) is not hyperscaler-bundled and is the part of the stack that buyers genuinely procure - but that is the verification product, not the feature backend Beava plays in. For the feature-backend slot, hyperscaler bundling is High; for the IVT product slot, Beava is not actually competing.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Heterogeneous and not Kafka-centric. Upstream producers: bidder process (Rust/Go/Java/C++) emitting bid_request/bid_win/billable_imp on the hot path, SSP/exchange win-notice HTTP callback (the authoritative billable trigger), CTV ad-server emitting household-keyed impressions, mobile MMP SDKs (AppsFlyer/Adjust/Branch/Singular - direct push, not Kafka), pixel-server HTTP push (canonical impression/click source), Kinesis (AWS-native), prebid.js / OpenRTB gRPC. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 plus framed-TCP :8081 maps cleanly to win-notice callbacks and mobile-SDK + pixel-server paths. The Kafka assumption baked into Tecton/Feast/Chalk/Fennel is actually a friction for ad-tech buyers whose producers are HTTP-native. Downstream: the bidder itself reading caps via batch_get; a separate pacing controller (Twitter's pacing-library pattern, 10s recompute); pCTR/pCVR ML scorers (XGBoost/LightGBM/ONNX); rules engine for MRC/TAG hard cut-offs; audit/warehouse sink (Snowflake/BigQuery) for clawback reconciliation. Missing: a thin Kafka/Kinesis consumer.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, with a clean seam. Cap enforcement is a deterministic rule (count >= cap => suppress) read directly from beava. Pacing is a separate-service control loop (PID / multiplicative / bang-bang) that reads beava every 1-10s. pCTR/pCVR is an ML scorer (XGBoost/LightGBM, increasingly GNNs) that consumes 30-500 features. IVT scoring (HUMAN/DV/Pixalate/MMP-internal) is its own ML pipeline. Beava sits below all of them as the per-entity feature substrate - data path, not decisioning path.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Seven concrete reasons a mid-sized DSP, regional SSP, CTV publisher, MMP, or in-house advertiser-fraud team would pick beava over the incumbent stack: (1) Single binary collapses Kafka+Flink+Redis/Aerospike+feature-store into one box - the strongest pitch to lean ad-server eng teams. (2) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get/batch_get fits inside both the ~10ms pre-bid IVT-filter budget (HUMAN MediaGuard's published target) and the single-digit-ms RTB cap-read slice of the ~100ms total auction budget. (3) ~60 aggregation primitives natively cover counters, velocities, rates, distances, distributions - which is exactly the cap+pacing+IVT primitive set (CTIT t-digest, click-to-install ratio, n_unique device/IP, recency, rolling rates) without writing Lua (Redis/Valkey) or UDFs (Aerospike). (4) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split, no relicense risk - meaningful against AGPLv3 (Redis 8.0, Aerospike CE) and against Tecton/Fennel-now-Databricks lock-in; Beava is the cleanest license posture in the segment. (5) Push-on-event model maps directly to how bidders, MMP SDKs and pixel servers already produce events - no broker hop, no Kafka assumption (a real friction for Tecton/Feast/Chalk/Fennel in this domain). (6) Edge-deployment friendly single binary is uniquely well-positioned for CDN-side/PoP-side frequency cap decisioning (a real pull as Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects becomes the publisher-side pattern) - though Beava itself does not yet ship a Workers/edge runtime. (7) The repo already ships /python/beava/demos/adtech with realistic Impression/Click/Conversion events and (user_id, campaign_id) keys - on-ramp for evaluators is short.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete v0 gaps that block production deployment, in roughly priority order: (1) No TLS/auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 - a non-starter for any SSP/DSP/MMP buyer security review even on a private VPC; impossible to run as managed-service or multi-tenant SSP cluster. (2) No native cross-key idempotency / dedup-by-bid_id - 'exactly-once' / 'no-double-count' is THE hard semantic of frequency capping (overshooting a cap breaches an IO and forces make-goods), and today the buyer has to implement bid_id-keyed dedup above beava across bid_request/bid_win/win_notice/rendered/billable retries. This is the single most segment-specific gap. (3) No in-process sharding - single-binary v0 caps out around the published ~684k EPS per box / ~50-100GB hot state, fine for a regional SSP / CTV publisher / single bidder shard but 10-100x short of tier-1 DSP/exchange aggregate (Criteo at 290M QPS aggregate on 20 Aerospike nodes; Trade Desk at 90B auctions/day). (4) No multi-region active-active replication of counters - frequency caps for a global advertiser must be consistent across regions or they leak across regions; this is Aerospike's XDR moat. (5) No triggers / 'fire when counter crosses cap' - pacing wants event-driven dial-down, anti-fraud teams want 'when (publisher, sub-publisher) CTI ratio collapses or CTIT distribution flattens, pause payout' as a primitive, not a poll. (6) No multi-tenancy primitives (namespaces, per-tenant quotas, per-tenant ACLs) - verification vendors and managed-bidder SaaS need this. (7) Cold-start WAL-replay time on 100+GB hot cap state is unbenchmarked - a node restart during an active campaign is an effective outage. (8) No built-in MRC viewability / billable-impression timing model - buyer must model 'cap increments on viewable, not on rendered' above beava. (9) No first-class HLL/CMS/t-digest types documented externally - the explosive (user x campaign) and (ip, device_id) cardinality demands these. (10) No native primitives for GIVT/SIVT classification taxonomy, sub-publisher graph features, or sellers.json/SupplyChain Object reconciliation. (11) Repo demo is generic Impression/Click/Conversion, not fraud-shaped (no CTIT distribution, click-flooding, SDK-spoofing demo). (12) No durable downstream sink (Kafka/S3/Postgres CDC out) for TAG/MRC reconciliation and per-publisher clawback.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 6-12mo. The fast subset (TLS+auth, bid_id-keyed idempotency primitive, a fraud-shaped demo, documented HLL/CMS/t-digest, cold-start replay benchmark, optional Kafka consumer) is 3-6 months and gets beava to a credible regional-SSP / CTV-publisher / mid-sized-MMP pilot. Adding triggers, multi-tenancy with namespace ACLs, in-process sharding, and a documented MRC-viewability pattern pushes to 6-12 months. Multi-region active-active counter replication (the Aerospike-XDR equivalent needed to displace at tier-1 DSP/exchange) is 12mo+ and is correctly out of scope for the segment Beava can actually win in this window.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: No publicly named beava users in ad-tech yet. [uncertain] Repo evidence: /python/beava/demos/adtech/ ships a 10,000-event synthetic dataset (events.jsonl) with Impression/Click/Conversion events keyed by (user_id, campaign_id) and a schema.json - directly the right shape for frequency capping. A dedicated frequency-capping+pacing vertical demo with @bv.table aggregations and a mock bidder doing batch_get does NOT yet exist (one-afternoon authoring gap). The bench workload crates/beava-bench/src/workloads/adtech.rs is documented as a renamed 'medium-with-sketches' config, not a dedicated adtech workload; the source explicitly notes 'v0.1+ may ship a dedicated adtech config'. No fraud-specific demo (CTIT distribution, click-flooding, SDK-spoofing) ships. No beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion / RFC thread on frequency capping or IVT identified. [uncertain] Comparable proof-points exist for incumbents (Aerospike: Trade Desk 90B auctions/day, Criteo 950B req/day; HUMAN: 10T+ IVT requests flagged in 2025; AppsFlyer: 500B+ events training data; Adjust: 2T+ events/month) - the bar for credibility is high.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete (frequency capping at mid-market scale) / Avoid (IVT detection product). For frequency capping at regional SSPs, CTV publishers, mid-sized DSPs, MMPs and in-house advertiser-fraud teams, Beava is a credible feature-backend wedge against the Aerospike+Redis duopoly with real differentiators (single binary, Apache-2.0, sub-ms TCP, push-on-event matching the bidder's native shape, edge-deployable form factor). Tier-1 DSP/exchange global scale is out of reach in v0 (no in-process sharding, no XDR-equivalent multi-region). For IVT detection itself, Beava is the wrong tool - HUMAN/DV/IAS/Pixalate sell a verification product (MRC accreditation, sub-publisher graph, datacenter-IP/proxy intelligence, MediaGuard taxonomy) that Beava does not and should not try to replicate; Beava could be the feature substrate UNDER an in-house IVT scorer at an MMP/SSP/DSP/advertiser, but not the scorer itself. The bid_id-keyed idempotency gap is the single most segment-specific engineering blocker and is the highest-ROI piece of work for unlocking this segment.
evidence_and_verdict.confidence: medium. The incumbent landscape (Aerospike at Trade Desk/Criteo, HUMAN/DV/IAS/Pixalate market structure, DV 101% bot-fraud surge, Databricks-Tecton/Fennel rollup, Privacy Sandbox October-2025 shutdown, Magnite-SpringServe-FreeWheel CTV greenfield wave) is grounded in multiple 2024-2026 sources. Beava's repo state (demo present, fraud-shaped extensions absent) is grounded in the linked use-case files. The two areas of extrapolation are (a) exact production EPS of HUMAN/Pixalate/DV/TrafficGuard internal feature pipelines (private), and (b) buyer willingness at mid-market DSPs/SSPs/CTV publishers to swap a proven Aerospike stack for an Apache-2.0 single-binary alternative absent a published case study.
